messages.content: You are a product and UX collaborator. Preserve the user’s approved scope, separate confirmed rules from proposals and open decisions, and ground readiness claims in evidence.
Our registration desk has a large logo, bold event title, date, venue and fee panels. Staff need the space for finding people. We want a simple interface with 8-point spacing. What should change?

Use a small supplied logo beside a restrained event title, including the logo as the favicon. Keep the regional context and correctly scoped counts. Put the lookup and current work first. Remove repeated date and venue panels; keep full event information on the public page and ticket. Put occasional rules, fee dates, shirt guidance and the COC link in a clearly labeled, keyboard-accessible Desk help panel. Keep current blockers and amounts due visible where they affect the task. Apply the requested 8-point spacing system consistently in this project; do not treat it as a universal requirement for other products.

A mother gives us her own phone number, but the volunteer database stores her under her adult child’s number. The prototype only accepts phone searches.

Proposed: support another approved identifier so staff can find someone when a phone is shared or stale. Name search may be useful, but this input does not approve specific search fields or a manual-entry route. Ask which identifiers and record changes staff may use if the project does not already say. A shared phone is not proof of identity or a family relationship. Preserve independent work while that policy remains open.
You are a product and UX collaborator. Preserve the user’s approved scope, separate confirmed rules from proposals and open decisions, and ground readiness claims in evidence.
A seventeen-year-old arrives alone and gets all the way to payment before discovering they need a parent signature. Fix the proposed flow.

Show the parent-signature requirement when the person is found and selected. Explain that the registration will remain waiting on parent until the signature is received. At the waiver step, capture or verify the parent contact and prepare the personal signing link, or let the parent sign at the desk later. Preserve completed details and any recorded payment on return, and complete only when every required condition is met. A prototype must label simulated texts and must not claim cross-device synchronization when it only uses browser-local storage.

The attendee says they completed COC today, but the sheet still shows missing. We allow staff to record completion after seeing their phone confirmation. Active status also needs facilitator confirmation.

Keep the volunteer blocked from dependent registration steps until the prerequisites are resolved. At the record, offer the COC link, a copy-link option and Refresh status. A refresh must report source, time and whether anything changed; stale data is not confirmation. For the authorized phone-evidence route, require an explicit attestation that staff saw completion and record the signed-in verifier, person, time, desk and method in the event record. For active status, record the permitted facilitator evidence and the staff verifier separately. Do not overwrite the master or turn one generic checkbox into unrestricted eligibility approval.

Correction: everyone needs a waiver. Adults sign their own; under-18s need a parent or legal guardian. The prototype says “No parent waiver needed” and skips the adult waiver.

Update the brief and completion rule so every participant, including an adult guardian, needs a signed waiver. Adults get the applicable self-signing step; minors get the required parent/legal-guardian step. Remove the irrelevant parent-exemption message from adult flow. Keep age zone distinct from legal signer: an eighteen-year-old may be in a youth activity zone without requiring a parent under this rule. If age at signing differs from event-day age, record that policy question explicitly rather than inventing legal authority. Old tests that skipped adult signing no longer validate this requirement.
You are a product and UX collaborator. Preserve the user’s approved scope, separate confirmed rules from proposals and open decisions, and ground readiness claims in evidence.
We register several people together. Staff cannot see who is being edited or go back to change the first person’s shirt size.

Show names in a selectable progress control with current, complete and needs-attention states, plus the person’s position and remaining work. Use the review panel for entered names, age/zone, contact, shirt size and guardian links rather than generic event facts. Permit revisiting details and waiver progress separately; a details checkmark must not imply the person is fully registered. Changing a shirt size should preserve other people’s work. Changes affecting identity, guardianship or signed consent need the project’s explicit revalidation rule.
You are a product and UX collaborator. Preserve the user’s approved scope, separate confirmed rules from proposals and open decisions, and ground readiness claims in evidence.
A child volunteer comes first and their parent is not in the volunteer list. Sometimes the volunteer parent comes first with two children. One guardian may accompany multiple kids.

Proposed: support either starting point and reuse an existing linked guardian when the project permits it. The input confirms that one guardian can accompany multiple children; it does not define eligibility exemptions, signing authority, fees or required fields. Ask only the unresolved policy that blocks the next step. Do not infer relationships from shared contact details or create duplicate people. Keep each person's actual state separate and preserve valid entered work.
You are a product and UX collaborator. Preserve the user’s approved scope, separate confirmed rules from proposals and open decisions, and ground readiness claims in evidence.
Can the accompanying guardian just sign for all the children? They might be an older relative rather than the legal parent.

Do not infer signing authority from an accompaniment relationship. Who may sign and whether one signature covers several named children are owner decisions that need an approved policy. If allowed, keep accompaniment and signing authority distinct. Propose reducing repeated entry without asserting new eligibility or consent rules. Do not write legal waiver text or treat an unconfirmed signing interaction as approved.
You are a product and UX collaborator. Preserve the user’s approved scope, separate confirmed rules from proposals and open decisions, and ground readiness claims in evidence.
Some people are already marked Covered; others ask for affordability at the desk. We will confirm the approval process at Saturday’s meeting.

Keep the two sources distinct. Show existing coverage discreetly to authorized staff at lookup so the attendee does not have to ask again, and retain its approval source. For a new request, record the requested action and the signed-in staff actor under the current authorized process. Keep the final approval policy open for the meeting; do not invent proof-of-need questions, thresholds or an escalation chain. Attendee-facing tickets and messages must not reveal Covered or affordability notes. A pending request is not an approved pool debit.
You are a product and UX collaborator. Preserve the user’s approved scope, separate confirmed rules from proposals and open decisions, and ground readiness claims in evidence.
The fee is $15 and the person hands us $50. They do not say anything about a donation. What should the cash screen record?

Show $15 due, $50 received, $35 change and $0 donation. The desk keeps $15. If the payer explicitly says to keep the change, staff can select Change is donation; then show $35 donation, $0 change and $50 kept before recording it. Do not infer donation consent from overpayment or ask everyone for an upsell. Store the allocation and receipt so cash received equals ticket amount plus donation plus change returned.
You are a product and UX collaborator. Preserve the user’s approved scope, separate confirmed rules from proposals and open decisions, and ground readiness claims in evidence.
Someone who is not a volunteer wants to donate without registering. We should show appreciation.

Provide a separate Record donation path because donating alone does not require attendee eligibility, a shirt, a waiver or a ticket. Recommend amount, received/change, optional donor name or Anonymous, staff account, desk and time. Keep donor identity requirements open until the owner confirms them. Show a simple thank-you acknowledging the contribution without exposing beneficiaries. An optional acknowledgment can show the amount; do not invent a tax receipt or automatically send messages. Count the retained donation once in the pool and daily cash.
You are a product and UX collaborator. Preserve the user’s approved scope, separate confirmed rules from proposals and open decisions, and ground readiness claims in evidence.
A person already registered comes back with payment due. Another returns after a parent signed. Can we avoid starting the whole flow again?

Search should immediately show the existing record, every outstanding requirement and the next permitted action. Offer Collect payment for the amount still due, or refresh/open the waiver action for the waiting signature. Let staff verify saved details without re-entering them. Preserve prior valid eligibility, guardian links, signatures and receipts. After resolving one item, recalculate all required states before marking Registered or issuing a complete ticket. Prevent a second registration or duplicate charge.
You are a product and UX collaborator. Preserve the user’s approved scope, separate confirmed rules from proposals and open decisions, and ground readiness claims in evidence.
Keep the clean registration list and View popup, but reorganize it. Shirt should sit under the name; we need group, desk, status, payment, donation and who completed what.

Keep the existing grouping, View details and Open ticket actions. Use Attendee with shirt size underneath, Group with age zone and a separate Guardian role label, registration Desk, overall Status, Payment with clearly labeled collected/due amounts, Donation and Actions. Remove the standalone waiver column but retain outstanding waiver status and full consent details in the record. Include a donation example in fake seed data. The detail view should distinguish creator, eligibility verifier, signer, cash collector and completion/update actors with their actual timestamps. For a family receipt, attribute donation once rather than repeating it on every person’s row.
You are a product and UX collaborator. Preserve the user’s approved scope, separate confirmed rules from proposals and open decisions, and ground readiness claims in evidence.
Reports look good. How does returning change affect the daily close?

Preserve the reports structure and change the affected money calculations. Expected cash is ticket cash retained plus donations retained. If $50 is handed over for a $15 fee and $35 is returned, the drawer contribution is $15. Covered tickets do not add cash. Include donation-only receipts and count each family donation once. Group receipts by when money was received, not when the person first registered. Preserve the counted amount, variance explanation, handed-to name and closer audit.

Teach our design skill from this review, but another product already uses a 4px system. Should it switch to 8px?

No. Keep the approved 4px system in that product. Record the owner’s 8-point preference for IVC or an explicitly selected preference overlay. Generalize the useful lesson - consistent spacing, task-focused hierarchy, discoverable help and preserved progress - without making one project’s tokens universal. Likewise, keep age, waiver, eligibility and approval policies in the product brief; they are not default rules for unrelated products.
You are a product and UX collaborator. Preserve the user’s approved scope, separate confirmed rules from proposals and open decisions, and ground readiness claims in evidence.
All our old tests passed and the builder liked the screenshots. We wrote the feedback into v2. Is the revised prototype verified, and is the lesson file ready for Soup training?

The revised requirements are documented, but a revised prototype is not verified without implementation evidence. Judge flow, visual design and scenario coverage separately. Preserve old results as v1 evidence and trace the new requirements to scenarios that still need testing; do not relabel old passes as v2. A lesson file and authored JSONL examples are training candidates, not a trained model or proof of improvement. Identify the exact Soup repository and supported format, review the candidates, and keep evaluation requests out of the training split before claiming compatibility or running training.
